projects.title: Wild Frontier
projects.description: Most mobile 4X games bury resource state under decoration. Wild Frontier puts it on a translucent HUD plate over a hex-gridded jungle map, color-codes every resource to a fixed palette, and replaces health bars with status badges — Ready, Moving, Fortified, Wounded — so a player reads what a settlement needs in under a second. Home HUD, map, build and unit systems designed mobile-first, one thumb, one action bar.

annotations.text: Terrain reads as a tactical grid, not a photo.

projects.title: Duo Git
projects.description: Most gamification punishes absence: a broken streak becomes a reason to quit rather than to return. DuoGit designs the fail state as part of the loop instead of the end of it — a character state machine with four states acknowledges a gap without judging it, and comeback mechanics are built in. Nine screens, a full HUD widget family for iOS and Android, league ranking and XP economy, a documented UI style guide, and retention metrics to check the system actually works: streak recovery rate, Day 7 retention, time-to-first-commit.

projects.title: Cuak
projects.description: Banking apps show balance, limit and due date but never answer the question users actually have: am I okay? Cuak promotes state to primary interface — a 60/40 layout gives objective data the left side and the character the right, six progression tiers turn behaviour into visible rank, and a simulator warns before the action instead of reporting after it. Playtested with five users: five of five read their situation faster from the character's state than from the same number shown alone.
